constraints: THREE-WAY, not two-way — a cold critic caught the two-way version contradicting the fail-closed rule. agent_id ABSENT means a top-level agent: bare session_id, unchanged behavior. agent_id PRESENT AND WELL-FORMED: session_id#agent_id. agent_id PRESENT BUT UNUSABLE (empty, non-string, or containing '#', '/', '\\' or '..'): return None and write NO binding at all. g4-implement.title: Live acceptance — a real trip from a per-agent reading: implement
g4-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer via scripts/run_crew.py. THIS GATE IS THE DELIVERABLE — the issue is not done until a trip is observed firing from a per-agent reading on a live run. Build a one-shot acceptance harness (kept runnable, NOT CI-wired, living OUTSIDE the repo in the scratchpad so it never enters the diff) and run it. Vehicle: a fresh headless `claude -p --settings <file>` whose settings wire THIS WORKTREE's hooks by absolute path, launched with its cwd in a disposable sandbox so CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR resolves to the sandbox and the main checkout's live store is never touched. That vehicle is already proven end to end — see evidence/probe-payloads.jsonl. Sandbox: real gated spines created by THIS worktree's checklist_engine.py, each with at least two gates so there is a real advance to refuse, plus a large plain-text corpus as genuine reading material. RUN SHAPE: (i) the PARENT claims its own spine too — not only the children — so the 'parent keeps its bare key' half of done-condition 1 is actually exercised rather than passing on an empty set; (ii) at least TWO subagents on a 1M-window model in MODEL_WINDOWS, each claiming its own spine, each consuming a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT amount of the corpus; (iii) ONE further subagent that claims NOTHING, to observe the coverage loss named in g3(e); (iv) ONE NESTED dispatch (a subagent that itself dispatches a subagent), because the probe only ever captured spawnDepth 1 while this project has 52 real depth-2 agents on disk — if a nested agent's payload names its parent AGENT's transcript rather than the root session's, the derivation yields a path that never exists and the governor is permanently, silently blind for every nested agent. Each agent runs the engine's current between chunks, reports its output verbatim, then attempts advance and reports verbatim whatever comes back. At least one agent must RELEASE, so the key-disappears-on-release claim is not tested on an empty set. Two arms, one variable: the control arm points the same settings at the main checkout's unmodified hooks.

g5-sweep.title: Sweep the stale bare-key bindings in the live store
g5-sweep.imperative: REASONING GATE, driven in the Commander's own context — no crew. Crew waiver reason: this mutates the MAIN CHECKOUT's live shared binding store while sibling runs of this same epic are in flight; the pre-clearance for that mutation was granted to this Commander by name in the launch order, it is not shippable code, and the script is deleted after its one run. Putting a crew inside live shared state is the larger risk, so the independent-eye finding is answered mechanically instead — see the constraints. Sequence, no step skippable: (1) DRY RUN — copy C:/Programs/constellation-skills/.agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json verbatim to evidence/binding-before.json, then emit evidence/binding-sweep-plan.md listing EVERY entry with its key, spine path, whether that spine file exists, its lease status, and KEEP or DROP with the reason; state the totals. (2) REAL RUN — re-read the file immediately before writing, re-evaluate the KEEP/DROP predicate against that fresh read rather than trusting the plan-time verdict, confirm nothing changed under you, then write atomically with the same tmp+os.replace discipline the hooks use. (3) VERIFY — snapshot to evidence/binding-after.json and assert the planned DROP set is gone and every KEEP entry survives byte-identical. (4) DELETE the sweeper; the commit notes it existed. The sweeper lives in the work area, never under scripts/.

triage_candidates.statement: spine_rail's agent_id check is a DENYLIST while gauge_writer_hook's is an ALLOWLIST, so they disagree by design: an agent_id like 'a:b' gets a binding written by spine_rail that the gauge writer will never resolve, leaving an orphaned dict entry. No filesystem hazard (confirmed at source by g2's reviewer: the binding key is only ever a dict key, never a path). The durable fix is moving the allowlist into spine_rail so one rule governs both. Not done here: spine_rail was closed and reviewed at g1, and the launch order's scope ruling says note-and-pass-up rather than reopen.

docs/agents/engine-config.json does not exist in this repo, yet every spine and plan template's config_ref points at it. The engine falls back silently, so the rework cap, replan policy and human checkpoints are all defaults nobody chose. Reported independently by three separate crews across this run.

git worktree add into the scratchpad fails on Windows MAX_PATH in this repo, so the standard isolate-the-revert move for a non-vacuity check needs a copy fallback. Worth carrying in the crew doctrine, since every gate in this run needed that measurement.

No mechanical link ties the gauge record's field count across its assertion sites. This run found SEVEN separate places asserting a four-field record, across docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md, gauge_writer_hook.py, gauge_reader.py and test_gauge_writer.py, and each was found by a different pass. A test importing gauge_reader.REQUIRED_FIELDS and asserting the document's field table against it would close the class; today the only thing keeping seven sites honest is that someone looks.

The binding store's read-modify-write takes no lock (spine_rail._save_json_map is atomic per write, but load-modify-save is not). Per-agent keying makes a dispatched wave write N entries where it previously wrote one, so the window widens exactly as the fan-out grows. A lost write reintroduces precisely the blindness #419 removes, and its symptom is silence — indistinguishable from an idle governor. Deliberately untested by this run (concurrency was out of scope); raised independently by two reviewers and one cold critic.

Dispatched agents read the engine's RAIL: banner as a possible prompt-injection attempt and said so in their transcripts during the acceptance run. Worth knowing: the rail is doctrine the engine pushes at the agent, and an agent that treats it as hostile input may discount the very instruction the rail exists to deliver.

The HARD refusal's remedy string ('Run: attach g1 --type refresh-request --field seam=g1 --field why_ref=<why-id>') assumes a Constellation-aware reader. An agent that trips without the corpus loaded gets an instruction it cannot act on, which is the #331 offered-and-declined question wearing a new hat.

g4-assert-control-output.txt does not regenerate from its own archived script: a trailing section was appended from a command that was not recorded. Every number in it reproduces, so this is an evidence-hygiene defect rather than a wrong claim, but an archived artifact that cannot be regenerated from its archived producer is not reproducible evidence.

MATERIAL SCOPE LIMIT ON THIS ISSUE'S WIN, found by the sweep's dry run. The binding store resolves a relative --file against the hook payload's cwd, and for an agent dispatched into a worktree that cwd is the MAIN CHECKOUT (issue #269: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is fixed at session launch). So a worktree-based agent's binding records a main-checkout path that does not exist: 60 of the 64 live entries were exactly this, including every spine of this very run's own crews. The gauge writer's _is_contained check passes on shape, and _atomic_write_json creates parent dirs, so the reading is written into a PHANTOM .agent-work/<work-id>/ inside the main checkout while the engine reads the worktree copy and sees nothing. #419's acceptance ran in a sandbox where cwd equalled the project dir, so it did not surface there. Per-agent identity is therefore proven for agents whose cwd is the project dir; for a worktree-dispatched agent the reading still lands in the wrong tree. This predates #419 and is orthogonal to it — the wrong path was recorded before this change too — but it is the next thing standing between the governor and firing on real Constellation runs.

The binding store accumulates junk keys from --file parsing: the swept set included entries keyed by literal 'C:\Programs\constellation-skills\$E' and '...\x', i.e. fragments of malformed or shell-mangled engine commands recorded as if they were spine paths. spine_rail._resolve_abs accepts whatever --file carried without checking it looks like a spine. Cheap guard: refuse to record a path that is not a .json.
